nodes.label: Technical Decision Log
nodes.rationale: Append-only record of every technical choice the specification did not dictate, each with alternatives considered and the reason. Newest last.

nodes.label: tsx for Development, No Build Step
nodes.rationale: tsx runs the ESM/NodeNext sources directly and watches without an intermediate dist/, keeping the workspace-to-workspace import path honest. No stage's acceptance criteria require a compiled artefact yet.

nodes.label: @pgp/shared Resolves to TypeScript Source
nodes.rationale: Pointing exports at ./src/index.ts means tsx, Vitest and tsc --noEmit all resolve the same files with no build ordering between workspaces. Cost: a compiled production build of api will need shared bundled or pre-built.

nodes.label: Split Liveness and Readiness Probes
nodes.rationale: Folding the database check into GET /health makes the probe unable to distinguish a dead process from a dead database, and makes npm test require a live database. GET /health/ready runs SELECT 1 instead. Prisma connects lazily so /health can still answer during an outage.

nodes.label: Two Database URLs: App Role and Owner Role
nodes.rationale: A revocation is meaningless if the application connects as the schema owner — an owner cannot be denied its own tables. DATABASE_URL is the least-privileged pgp_app role; DATABASE_MIGRATION_URL is pgp_owner, reached through Prisma's directUrl so no wrapper script is needed.

nodes.label: Argon2id Parameters Pinned in Code
nodes.rationale: m=65536, t=3, p=2 taken from the security specification. Making them environment-tunable adds a way to silently weaken password hashing via misconfiguration and buys nothing, so they are deliberately absent from .env.example.

nodes.label: Membership Numbers from a PostgreSQL Sequence
nodes.rationale: Computing MAX(memberNumber)+1 in application code races: two administrators creating a member at the same moment both read the same maximum. member_number_seq plus next_member_number() returning PG-0004 makes that impossible and keeps the format in one place.

nodes.label: CHECK Constraints for Invariants Prisma Cannot Express
nodes.rationale: minGuests/maxGuests coherence, positive party size, percentages within 0-100, outlet required on OUTLET_STAFF, and a reversal not pointing at itself are cheap in the database and cannot then be bypassed by a bug in a handler. A backstop, not the rule.

nodes.label: Member.tokenVersion Added Beyond the Build Plan
nodes.rationale: The build plan gives tokenVersion to StaffUser only, but the security document lists membership suspension among the events that must force re-authentication and names token version as the mechanism. Prime directive 3 gives the security document precedence; recorded as a deviation rather than a silent schema change.

nodes.label: HS256 Access Tokens Within a Single Deployable
nodes.rationale: The security document prefers EdDSA/RS256 but explicitly permits HS256 within a single deployable. This build is one Fastify process serving all surfaces. Revisit if the API is split, at which point asymmetric signing lets each verifier work without holding the signing secret.

nodes.label: Refresh Tokens Hashed with SHA-256
nodes.rationale: A refresh token is 256 bits of server-generated randomness, not a low-entropy human secret. Argon2id's deliberate slowness defends nothing and adds per-request latency; the only property needed is unlinkability from a DB leak, which SHA-256 provides.

nodes.label: OTP Codes Hashed with HMAC-SHA256
nodes.rationale: A 6-digit OTP is a ~20-bit space, trivially brute-forced offline at any hash speed, so a slow hash buys nothing. The real defenses are the 5-minute TTL and 5-attempt lockout. HMAC keyed by OTP_CODE_HMAC_SECRET still prevents rainbow-table matching against a leaked table.

nodes.label: In-Memory Two-Dimensional Rate Limiter
nodes.rationale: Limiting per IP and per identifier at once on the same route is not directly expressible with a single off-the-shelf plugin instance. A ~40-line fixed-window module was simpler to get exactly right. Known limitation: limits reset on restart and are not shared across processes.

nodes.label: R17 Enforced by an onRoute Hook
nodes.rationale: A registration wrapper only protects routes that remember to use it — a plain app.get() slips straight past, which is precisely the failure the security document describes. Fastify's onRoute hook fires for every route however registered, so there is no bypass to remember.

nodes.label: scopedWhere Instead of Spreading the Scope Fragment
nodes.rationale: The security document's illustrative spread is only safe while the fragment shares no keys with the base query. A member's scope is { id: their own id }, so the later spread wins and every lookup returned the caller's own record instead of 404. AND composition cannot clobber.

nodes.label: 403 for a Route, 404 for an Out-of-Scope Record
nodes.rationale: The reasoning for 404 is specifically that a 403 confirms the record exists — it is about records. Which endpoints exist is not a secret (they are in the client bundle), so a 403 on a route leaks nothing.

nodes.label: Exhaustive Role Matrix, No Wildcard
nodes.rationale: A wildcard for ADMINISTRATOR means every permission added later is granted silently at the moment it is defined rather than when someone decides it should be. Listing all of them makes each grant a deliberate edit, and the matrix test fails if catalogue and expectations drift apart.

nodes.label: Fetch-Then-Check Enforced by Source Scanning
nodes.rationale: It is a property of how handlers are written, not something a running server can be asked about. fetch-then-check.test.ts scans src/routes for Prisma reads of scoped models and requires a scope fragment in the same statement, with an exempt list carrying written reasons. The guard resolves a where passed as a variable within a 25-line lookbehind.

nodes.label: 160-Bit Crockford Base32 Claim Codes
nodes.rationale: The wireframe's PG- ____ - ____ placeholder is roughly 40 bits, guessable at the rate an activation endpoint could be driven. The security document requires at least 128 bits and forbids deriving the code from the membership number. Crockford excludes I, L, O and U and input is normalised for 1/I and 0/O confusions.

nodes.label: Consent Records a Declined Channel Explicitly
nodes.rationale: Writing nothing for a refusal makes 'declined' and 'never asked' indistinguishable a year later, which is exactly the question a complaint would raise. Both channels are required in the claim payload so an omission is never silently read as consent.

nodes.label: Suspension Increments tokenVersion and Revokes Refresh Families
nodes.rationale: A status check alone leaves an already-issued access token valid until it expires — up to 30 minutes for a member. Refresh tokens are separate server-side state and are revoked explicitly, or the member could mint a fresh access token seconds later.

nodes.label: Passcodes Delivered by Email over SMTP
nodes.rationale: The client answered 'Gmail over SMTP'. Gmail cannot send SMS and no email-to-SMS gateway serves +974, so the substance was implemented by treating email as the channel: the phone number stays the identifier and the server looks up the stored address. Explicitly interim and weaker than SMS — whoever controls the mailbox controls the membership.

nodes.label: MFA Scope Resolved from the Narrower Sentence
nodes.rationale: The security document says both 'mandatory on every dashboard account, without exception' and 'MFA for any staff account that can reach more than the verification page'. The second is the specific statement and resolves the first. TOTP via otplib, secret encrypted with AES-256-GCM, ten Argon2id-hashed single-use recovery codes.

nodes.label: Design Tokens in packages/ui, Not Tailwind
nodes.rationale: CSS custom properties consumed by all clients, each app overriding only semantic colour tokens. Chosen over Tailwind mainly for Stage 22: with CSS logical properties throughout, Arabic RTL costs one dir attribute rather than a per-class audit across three apps. Build-plan rule 1 (no styling) was retired deliberately, and no-styling.test.ts was renamed rather than deleted so its two load-bearing assertions survived.

nodes.label: Admin Overview Screen and Measured Charts
nodes.rationale: The dashboard opened on a hundred-row member table while the headline figures sat behind a tab. Benefit names are nominal so every bar wears one hue and there is no legend; reach is a meter not a doughnut. Colours were chosen by measuring contrast — --c-primary-soft measures 1.13:1 on white and is unusable as a meter track. Two silent defects found: the insufficient_data sentinel rendering into a KPI tile, and report rows mistyped as MemberRow.

nodes.label: Discount Rate Recorded on the Redemption
nodes.rationale: Reading the rate back from the Benefit put R14 (editable percentages) in silent conflict with reporting: moving dining from 25% to 20% restated every month already reported, and a member's own history contradicted their receipt. discountPctApplied and benefitVersion are NOT NULL with no default, so every creation site must state a rate. A reversal copies the original's rate rather than re-reading the benefit.

nodes.label: Benefit Request Replaces the Guest QR
nodes.rationale: Q1 answered: the client did not want a scanned credential. BenefitRequest PENDING -> APPROVED/DECLINED -> FULFILLED, with Benefit.outletKind routing approvals as data rather than a code mapping. A member cannot approve their own request because requests:create is a MEMBER permission and requests:decide a STAFF one. react-qr-code was kept in web-admin for otpauth:// enrollment. Later reversed on 2026-08-12.

nodes.label: The Verification Page Is Deleted
nodes.rationale: No counter application: an administrator records every redemption from the dashboard. Recording moved to POST /admin/redemptions with a required outletId, because an administrator at a desk cannot have the outlet inferred and a redemption attributed to the wrong outlet is worse than one attributed to none. The verification session went with it — a genuine reduction in control, acceptable only because every role that can now record already holds members:read.

nodes.label: Refresh Token Moves to an httpOnly Cookie
nodes.rationale: A module-scoped variable cost a sign-in on every page reload. The cookie is held by the browser rather than the page, so it survives a reload and document.cookie cannot see it. No CSRF token because SameSite=Strict, Path=/auth/refresh and an unreadable cross-origin response close the gap together — a CSRF token becomes necessary the moment any state-changing route authenticates by cookie.

nodes.label: Google Sheets as a Sanitised One-Way Mirror
nodes.rationale: Replacing PostgreSQL was rejected: the programme depends on transactions, uniqueness, idempotency, immutable redemptions and security records Sheets cannot enforce. A repeatable-read full snapshot publishes every five minutes outside all request handlers, so Google latency cannot fail a member creation. Treated as a standing bulk export, so the existing export policy holds: membership numbers may leave, names/phones/emails may not.

nodes.label: One Hotel-Facing Account Type: Administrator
nodes.rationale: Client confirmed the required product is the member guest app plus the administrator panel. The role selector is removed rather than hidden and the server sets the role instead of trusting a request field. Legacy rows are suspended rather than converted, because converting them would turn a later reinstatement into privilege escalation.

nodes.label: The Benefit Request Becomes a Notice
nodes.rationale: BenefitRequest is the guest announcing themselves; Redemption is the immutable record a discount was given. Removing the administrator in the middle leaves SENT -> FULFILLED with NOT_USED as the other ending. Creating requests as APPROVED was rejected as a smaller diff that would put the word 'approved' in the audit log for something nobody approved. The one-per-minute throttle counts rows on requestedAt so a deploy does not hand anybody a fresh allowance.

nodes.label: Outlet Accounts Authenticating Through Google
nodes.rationale: Real OAuth with the ID token verified against Google's published keys — issuer, audience, nonce and email_verified all checked. Google authenticates, the application authorizes: both the hosted-domain gate and an active OUTLET_STAFF row must pass. Cannot enforce whether the account's own 2FA is switched on, which Google does not disclose. Superseded by per-device tokens later the same day.

nodes.label: Per-Device Outlet Tokens
nodes.rationale: Google's operational dependencies (OAuth client, Workspace mailboxes, shared-account 2FA policy) cannot be completed by deploying this application. pgo_ tokens carry 256 bits of entropy, are stored only as a unique SHA-256 digest, and are accepted only by POST /outlet/auth/token. One token per physical device makes the blast radius the device's one outlet. Explicitly one factor, accepted for the pilot.

nodes.label: Outlet Authentication Is Device-Token-Only
nodes.rationale: An outlet account means the labelled counter device, not a mailbox. No Google button, OAuth callback, password login, allowlist or secondary path. Outlet.notifyEmail has exactly one job — notifications — and is not copied into StaffUser or used to recover a token. Local login is deliberately the production login: the development session-bundle helper is removed so a JWT bundle cannot be mistaken for the standing credential.

nodes.label: WhatsApp Considered and Rejected
nodes.rationale: Automatic WhatsApp means Meta's Cloud API: verified business account, dedicated number, pre-approved templates and a per-message fee; the free wa.me link needs a human to press it. The destination is the outlet's own screen instead. One deliberate departure from the redaction policy: an outlet notice carries the membership number and benefit because it is useless without them — a difference of audience, and the guest's name is still never sent.

nodes.label: Static QR on the Printed Card, Q1 Reversed
nodes.rationale: A printed payload has one timestamp for the life of the card, so a freshness window either rejects the card on day two or is not a freshness window. v2.<member_ref>.<hmac> is static and says so in the version prefix; v1 remains implemented so rotation can be reinstated without reprinting. Acceptable only because the code identifies and grants nothing (R10) — no stronger than the membership number already printed on the front. Derived from the opaque internal id, never the sequential PG- number.

nodes.label: Dashboard Refreshes Through One Shared Promise
nodes.rationale: The admin landing screen opens with five requests at once, so ten minutes after sign-in all five 401'd together and rotated the same cookie in parallel: the first won, the other four read as replay, and the family died. A twelve-hour refresh token destroyed by a ten-minute access token. The server was left alone deliberately — widening rotation would weaken theft detection to compensate for a client defect.

nodes.label: STAFF_MFA_REQUIRED Development Switch
nodes.rationale: Defaults to true; anything but the exact string 'false' is true so a typo fails closed; and loadEnv refuses to return if it is false while NODE_ENV=production — a boot failure rather than a warning. Nothing is deleted when it is off. A password-only sign-in audits as auth.mfa.skipped, never auth.login.success, because a trail that recorded them identically would hide the only rows that could evidence a misconfiguration.

nodes.label: Breached-Password Screening via HIBP k-Anonymity
nodes.rationale: Five characters of the SHA-1 leave the process, several hundred suffixes come back, the comparison happens locally. Fails open on a network error and logs that it did, because an outage must not stop somebody changing a password — the passwords people most urgently want to change are the ones already compromised.

nodes.label: Shared Caddy api_proxy Snippet with CIDR Restriction Inside
nodes.rationale: Both clients hardcode BASE = '/api' but the production Caddyfile proxied nothing, so every production API call would have returned the HTML document and the apps would have loaded then silently failed. Fixing it opened a hole — proxying /api/* on my.<domain> would expose /api/admin/* publicly — so the CIDR restriction now lives inside the shared snippet, safe to import anywhere rather than safe only where somebody remembered to pair it with a guard.

nodes.label: CSV Export with BOM and Unconditional Quoting
nodes.rationale: The export returned JSON that finance — the one audience it exists for — could not open. Now text/csv with a Content-Disposition filename carrying discount_pct (the rate applied on that visit) and a computed discount_value. Quoting is unconditional because an outlet called 'Crust, Doha' would shift every column after it, and Excel reads a UTF-8 file without a BOM as the local codepage.

nodes.label: /admin/staff Management Endpoints
nodes.rationale: StaffUser.tokenVersion and status were the mechanism behind instant revocation, both worked, and no endpoint reached either — so offboarding was a manual UPDATE against production. Three refusals: you cannot suspend yourself, suspend the last active administrator, or reset your own second factor. Never-your-own is the enforceable half of two-person control without causing permanent lockout at a hotel with one administrator.

both argue a uniformly random server-generated secret needs a fast digest, not a slow password hash
both replace a control somebody must remember to apply with one that cannot be bypassed
both insist an explicit negative and a mere absence must never be recorded identically (declined vs never asked; auth.mfa.skipped vs auth.login.success)
both stop a derived, aggregate-looking surface becoming an indirect route to individual member movements
complementary halves of one identifier design: the public number is deliberately sequential, so every credential must be independent of it
